steps.body: A **cone** with the same base and height as a cylinder holds exactly **one-third** as much. So its volume is **V = ⅓πr²h** — the cylinder formula times a third. Three cones fill one matching cylinder.

predict.prompt: A cone and a cylinder share the same radius 3 and height 4. How does the cone's volume compare?

options.label: Exactly one third of the cylinder's
The same — same radius, same height

predict.reveal: A cone tapers to a point, so it holds far less than the cylinder around it — and the amount is not roughly a third but EXACTLY a third. Three cones empty into their cylinder and fill it precisely.

widget.prompt: Set the radius and height until the cone's volume reads 12π. Compare it with the cylinder that shares those measurements.
widget.successFeedback: 12π — and a cylinder with the same radius 3 and height 4 holds 36π. The cone is exactly a third of it. That is what the ÷ 3 in the formula is: three cones fill their cylinder.
widget.lowFeedback: Still under 12π. Try widening the radius before raising the height.
widget.highFeedback: Over 12π. Ease the radius back — it counts twice over.

steps.body: The reliable method: find the matching cylinder's volume (πr²h) first, then divide by 3. For r = 6, h = 5: cylinder is 36 × 5 = 180, and the cone is 180 ÷ 3 = 60, so V = 60π.

widget.prompt: A cone has radius 6 and height 5. What is its volume as a number times π?

commonErrors.feedback: That's the CYLINDER volume — the cone is a third: 180 ÷ 3 = 60.

widget.prompt: Why is a cone's volume one-third of the cylinder's?

panels.title: Same base, same height
panels.body: Picture a cone and a cylinder with the exact same circular base and the same height.

panels.title: Pour test
panels.body: If you fill the cone with water and pour it into the cylinder, it takes exactly THREE cone-fills to fill the cylinder.

panels.title: Conclusion
panels.body: So the cone holds one-third of the cylinder: V = ⅓πr²h.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly — three cones fill the matching cylinder, so a cone is one-third.

explanationVariants: The matching cylinder is 90π, so the cone is 90 ÷ 3 = 30π.

widget.prompt: A cone matches a cylinder of volume 90π. What is the cone's volume as a number times π?

commonErrors.feedback: That's the cylinder — the cone is a third: 90 ÷ 3 = 30.
The cone is SMALLER (one-third), so divide: 90 ÷ 3 = 30, not multiply.

widget.fallbackFeedback: A cone is one-third of its matching cylinder: 90 ÷ 3 = 30π.

explanationVariants: An ice-cream cone with radius 3 and height 6: cylinder = π × 9 × 6 = 54π, cone = 54 ÷ 3 = 18π.

widget.prompt: An ice-cream cone has radius 3 and height 6. What is its volume as a number times π?

commonErrors.feedback: That's the matching cylinder — the cone is a third: 54 ÷ 3 = 18.

hints: First find the matching cylinder: πr²h = π × 3² × 6.
That's π × 9 × 6 = 54π. The cone is one-third of it.

takeaways: V = ⅓πr²h — find πr²h, then divide by 3.
Three cones exactly fill a cylinder with the same base and height.
The cone is always smaller — divide, don't multiply.
